thread.title: Huami: Initial Mi Band 3 Sales Data Pointing To 2018 Outperformance - Huami Corporation (NYSE:HMI)

author: Pinxter Analytics
title: Huami: Initial Mi Band 3 Sales Data Pointing To 2018 Outperformance - Huami Corporation (NYSE:HMI)
text:
Arbitrage Thesis In a recent press release , Huami ( HMI ) announced it has sold over 1M Mi Band 3 wearable smartwatches in just 17 days, far outpacing the 2-month time frame it took for the Mi Band 2 in 2016 and the 3-month time frame for the Mi Band 1 in 2014. Most online retailers selling the Mi Bad 3 as a Xiaomi ( XI ) product have indicated they're sold out as the new product is flying off the shelves.
The company set the initial price of the Mi Band 3 at $25.99, higher than $22.99 it first sold the Mi Band 2 and with more than double the sales volume (so far) the company should report a near doubling of revenues as they are gearing up to release their Q2 financial figures on August 29th, 2018. Notably, the company guided for a ~34.5% revenue growth rate for the quarter, clearly not anticipating the success of the new release, and analysts expect the company to report roughly $105 million in revenues for the quarter.
Brief Overview A full and comprehensive overview of the company's business model and an industry overview including risks and rewards associated with their Xiaomi partnership and a comparative analysis to FitBit ( FIT ) can be found in my original investment thesis Huami: The Number One Global Wearables Market Player At A Discount .
Huami has a distribution agreement for their devices with Xiaomi, a recently-public mobile smartphone maker in China that includes a 19.3% stake in Huami, which means the success of the company is highly leveraged to their own in the wearables market. As global wearable technologies are set to increase at a 25% CAGR through 2021, Huami is capitalizing on these shifts, notably in China, where an estimate of 21% of smartphone users use a wearable device, higher than in the United States.
The rapid rise in sales are indicative of sustained market share capture as users in countries in the Asia-Pacific region seek a cheaper alternative to the high-priced Apple ( AAPL ) and Samsung ( OTC:SSNLF ) smart watches.
Headline Analysis Yesterday, the company released data on the unit sales figures of it's new product, the Mi Band 3, and stated that it sold over 1M units in just 17 days. The Mi Band 2, released in 2016, took 2 months to achieve the 1M units mark and the Mi Band 1, released in 2014, took over 3 months to do the same.
This represents nearly 4x the speed to achieve the same number of sales. It's hard to peg if this rate of sales will continue but the high demand on initial launch has been indicative of overall success with companies like Apple, Samsung and other technology companies, which remains bullish for Huami.
Price Per Unit Not only does the company expect a larger number of units to be sold, they also hiked the price per average unit from the Mi Band 2's $38.00 to $58.00 for the Mi Band 3, a 52% hike, which means even if they sell the same number of devices throughout 2018 revenues should see a considerable bounce. These figures are shown in multiple selling avenues across the internet and in countries like China and India, when looking at average prices including certain ad-ons and fitness features.
This is what leads to my estimate for revenue growth, assuming you take into account a steady growth rate for the company's Amazfit products, which account for roughly 20% of revenues. I therefore believe the company can easily show a 60% growth in sales for the year, higher than the current analysts estimates of 49%.
The company's gross margins should improve as well as they continue to work on reducing overall costs with supply chain initiatives and lower overhead costs, as they've shown in the most recent quarter.
(Source: Company Q1 Slides )
A Note: Xiaomi's Underwhelming IPO Even as Xiaomi's IPO underwhelmed some investors , pricing at the lower end of the range, the company's product sales remain robust and the wearables partnership is among them. As mentioned and analyzed in my previous article, this continued outperformance in sales and ability to manipulate unit prices without losing customers should secure a partnership renewal come the 2020 expiration or may amount to the opportunity for Xiaomi to buy Huami outright to enjoy a higher share of revenue contributions.
Price Hikes and Investment Conclusion As recent news points to an outstanding start of the new product launch of the Mi Band 3, current market estimates still call for a lower growth rate in revenues for the company as their unit sales timeframe nearly quadruple to 17 days from 2 months of the previous version.
Furthermore, the price hike from around $30.00 to $40.00 per average unit will aid revenue and net income growth as they continue to work on supply chain efficiency to reduce overall costs and improve gross margins. The lower price than competitors like Apple's and Samsung's version allow the company to continue and experiment with price hikes without hurting its sales avenues in the Asia-Pacific region and boost profits for future R&D initiatives. This is indicative from the price difference of $26.00 for the current model from the $16.00 for the Mi Band 1, even as more features are added, as the company has much lower manufacturing costs with better supply chains and still enjoys the marketing efforts of Xiaomi to launch their products.
Current expectations, I believe, don't account for this unit sales outperformance and unit price hike when looking at the 49% revenue growth rate expectation for the year as they remain a market leader, gaining market share throughout 2018. A near-term upward revision to earnings expectations or a clear and easy headline revenue and EPS beat can offer investors a prime news-arbitrage opportunity and long term investors, I believe, now have a clearer understanding of the demand in China and the company's ability to achieve meaningful long-term growth via price and technology manipulation.
Disclosure: I am/we are long HMI.
